name: CDS
frequency: Twice a year (CDS I and CDS II)
approxCandidates: ≈2–4 lakh applicants per cycle (approx.); about 450–460 vacancies per cycle across IMA, INA, AFA and OTA
eligibility: Graduate. INA needs an engineering degree, and AFA needs a degree with Physics and Maths at Class 12 or an engineering degree. Age is about 19–25 depending on the academy, unmarried for IMA/INA/AFA

notification.summary: CDS (II) 2026 was held on 13 September 2026, and its written result is expected in October 2026. Per UPSC's Calendar 2027, the CDS (I) 2027 notification is due on 2 December 2026 (applications until 22 December 2026) and the exam on 11 April 2027. Dates are provisional; upsc.gov.in itself could not be reached from the research sandbox.

pattern.notes: There are three papers of 2 hours and 100 marks each. English and GK have 120 questions each (100/120 ≈ 0.83 marks per question) and Elementary Maths has 100 (1 mark each). A wrong answer costs one-third of the question's marks. OTA (SSC) candidates take only English and GK (200 marks). The SSB interview follows. The bank holds 60 items, 20 per paper; for a short mock, score each paper with its own per-question marks as given in sections[].marking.

trendAnalysis.summary: English is moderate. Error spotting, comprehension and sentence or part ordering are about half the paper, and the vocabulary items (synonyms, antonyms, idioms) are of mid-level difficulty. GK is the most unpredictable paper: History, Geography and Polity are the static core, science is mostly Physics and Biology basics, and there are many questions on current affairs, defence exercises and international organisations. Elementary Maths stays at Class 10 level with an even spread across arithmetic, algebra, geometry, mensuration and trigonometry, but it is lengthy. Over 2024–26, GK difficulty has been moderate-to-tough while Maths and English stayed moderate.

resources.notes: UPSC posts CDS question papers on upsc.gov.in under Previous Question Papers. Answer keys are released only after the final result of that cycle.

questions.question:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error.
Each of the candidates (A) / have been given (B) / a separate room. (C) / No error (D)
questions.explanation: 'Each of' takes a singular verb, so part B should read 'has been given'.

questions.question:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error.
She has been working here (A) / for the last five years (B) / and is knowing everyone. (C) / No error (D)
questions.explanation: 'Know' is a stative verb and is not normally used in the continuous form, so part C should read 'and knows everyone'.

questions.question:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error.
Neither of the two answers (A) / is correct, so (B) / we must try again. (C) / No error (D)
questions.explanation: 'Neither of' takes a singular verb ('is'), so the sentence is correct.

questions.question:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error.
Despite of the heavy rain (A) / the match (B) / was completed on time. (C) / No error (D)
questions.explanation: 'Despite' is not followed by 'of'. Use 'Despite the heavy rain' or 'In spite of the heavy rain'.

questions.question: Choose the word most nearly SAME in meaning to OSTENSIBLE.
questions.explanation: Ostensible means apparent or seeming on the surface, though perhaps not actually so.

questions.question: Choose the word most nearly SAME in meaning to LACONIC.
questions.explanation: Laconic means using very few words, that is, terse.

questions.question: Choose the word most nearly OPPOSITE in meaning to OBDURATE.
questions.explanation: Obdurate means stubbornly refusing to change, so its opposite is yielding. The other options are near-synonyms.

questions.question: Choose the word most nearly OPPOSITE in meaning to EPHEMERAL.
questions.explanation: Ephemeral means short-lived, so its opposite is everlasting. The other three options are synonyms.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: The veteran's account of the war was so ______ that many in the audience were moved to tears.
questions.explanation: Poignant means evoking a keen sense of sadness, which fits 'moved to tears'.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: He is senior ______ me by two years.
questions.explanation: Comparatives of Latin origin such as senior, junior, superior and prior take 'to', not 'than'.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: The thief was caught ______ the act.
questions.explanation: The idiom is 'caught in the act'.

questions.question:
Choose the best replacement for the underlined part. If none is needed, choose 'No improvement'.
'The officer insisted on me to stay back.' (underlined: insisted on me to stay)
questions.explanation: 'Insist' is followed by 'on + gerund' ('insisted on my staying') or a that-clause ('insisted that I stay'). Of the options, only 'insisted that I stay' is correct.

questions.question:
Choose the best replacement for the underlined part. If none is needed, choose 'No improvement'.
'The number of cadets who passed the test are higher this year.' (underlined: are higher)
questions.explanation: 'The number of …' is singular and the sentence is in the present ('this year'), so 'is higher' is correct.

questions.question:
Arrange P, Q and R in the correct order to complete the sentence:
'The importance of ______.'
P: cannot be overstated
Q: regular physical training
R: for a soldier
questions.explanation: 'The importance of regular physical training (Q) for a soldier (R) cannot be overstated (P).'

questions.question:
Arrange the parts to form a meaningful sentence:
P: the river
Q: after heavy rain
R: overflowed its banks
S: in the hills
questions.explanation: 'The river (P) overflowed its banks (R) after heavy rain (Q) in the hills (S).' The other sequences are ungrammatical.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer the question.
'Military historians often observe that battles are seldom won by numbers alone. An army that is well supplied, well led and confident of its purpose can defeat a larger force that lacks these qualities. Leadership, in this view, is less about issuing orders than about earning trust: soldiers willingly follow a commander who shares their hardships and explains the reasons behind difficult decisions. Such trust cannot be created on the eve of battle; it is built slowly, through countless small acts of fairness in peacetime.'
Which of the following best expresses the central idea of the passage?
options: Commanders should avoid explaining their decisions
Effective leadership rests on trust earned over time
questions.explanation: The passage argues that leadership means earning trust built over time. It rejects the idea that numbers alone decide battles.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer the question.
'Military historians often observe that battles are seldom won by numbers alone. An army that is well supplied, well led and confident of its purpose can defeat a larger force that lacks these qualities. Leadership, in this view, is less about issuing orders than about earning trust: soldiers willingly follow a commander who shares their hardships and explains the reasons behind difficult decisions. Such trust cannot be created on the eve of battle; it is built slowly, through countless small acts of fairness in peacetime.'
According to the passage, how is trust between a commander and soldiers built?
options: Through many small acts of fairness in peacetime
By increasing the size of the army
questions.explanation: The last sentence says trust 'is built slowly, through countless small acts of fairness in peacetime'.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer the question.
'Military historians often observe that battles are seldom won by numbers alone. An army that is well supplied, well led and confident of its purpose can defeat a larger force that lacks these qualities. Leadership, in this view, is less about issuing orders than about earning trust: soldiers willingly follow a commander who shares their hardships and explains the reasons behind difficult decisions. Such trust cannot be created on the eve of battle; it is built slowly, through countless small acts of fairness in peacetime.'
The word 'seldom', as used in the passage, most nearly means:
questions.explanation: Seldom means rarely: battles are rarely won by numbers alone.

questions.question: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom: 'to bury the hatchet'
questions.explanation: To bury the hatchet is to end a quarrel and make peace.

questions.question: Choose the correct meaning of the phrase: 'a blessing in disguise'
options: Something that seems bad at first but turns out to be good
questions.explanation: A blessing in disguise is an apparent misfortune that later proves beneficial.

questions.question: The Buland Darwaza at Fatehpur Sikri was built by:
questions.explanation: Akbar built the Buland Darwaza (c. 1575–76) to commemorate his Gujarat campaign.

questions.question: The 'Arthashastra' is attributed to:
questions.explanation: The Arthashastra, a treatise on statecraft, is attributed to Kautilya (Chanakya), adviser to Chandragupta Maurya.

questions.question: The Swaraj Party was founded in 1923 by:
options: Bal Gangadhar Tilak and Annie Besant
G. K. Gokhale and M. G. Ranade
C. R. Das and Motilal Nehru
questions.explanation: C. R. Das and Motilal Nehru formed the Congress-Khilafat Swaraj Party in 1923 to contest council elections.

questions.question: Which of the following rulers was NOT part of the alliance that fought the English East India Company at the Battle of Buxar (1764)?
questions.explanation: At Buxar the Company fought the combined forces of Mir Qasim, Shuja-ud-Daula (Nawab of Awadh) and the Mughal emperor Shah Alam II. Haider Ali of Mysore was not involved.

questions.question: Which is the longest river of peninsular India?
questions.explanation: The Godavari (about 1,465 km) is the longest peninsular river and is often called the Dakshin Ganga.

questions.question: The 'Doldrums' are associated with which pressure belt?
questions.explanation: The doldrums are the calm equatorial low-pressure zone where the trade winds converge (the ITCZ).

questions.question: Which one of the following neighbouring countries of India is landlocked?
questions.explanation: Bhutan has no coastline. Myanmar and Bangladesh have coasts and Sri Lanka is an island.

questions.question: The idea of Directive Principles of State Policy in the Indian Constitution was borrowed from the Constitution of:
questions.explanation: The Directive Principles were inspired by the Irish Constitution, which itself drew on the Spanish Constitution.

questions.question: Who presides over a joint sitting of the two Houses of Parliament?
questions.explanation: Under Article 118(4), the Speaker of the Lok Sabha presides over a joint sitting called under Article 108.

questions.question: Article 32 of the Constitution of India deals with:
questions.explanation: Article 32 lets a person approach the Supreme Court to enforce Fundamental Rights. Dr Ambedkar called it the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution.

questions.question: The GDP deflator is the ratio of:
questions.explanation: GDP deflator = (nominal GDP / real GDP) × 100. It is a broad measure of the price level.

questions.question: The central office (headquarters) of the Reserve Bank of India is located in:
questions.explanation: The RBI was set up in Kolkata in 1935 and moved its central office permanently to Mumbai in 1937.

questions.question: The image formed by a convex mirror of a real object is always:
questions.explanation: A convex mirror always forms a virtual, erect and diminished image behind the mirror, which is why it is used as a rear-view mirror.

questions.question: A wave has a frequency of 500 Hz and a wavelength of 0.68 m. Its speed is:
Which one of the following is NOT an allotrope of carbon?
questions.explanation: Carborundum is silicon carbide (SiC), a compound, not an allotrope. Diamond, graphite and fullerenes are allotropes of carbon.

questions.question: Malaria is caused by:
questions.explanation: Malaria is caused by Plasmodium species and transmitted by female Anopheles mosquitoes.

questions.question: Which part of the human brain is mainly responsible for maintaining balance and coordinating voluntary movements?
questions.explanation: The cerebellum coordinates posture, balance and voluntary muscle activity.

questions.question: Which of the following is primarily responsible for depletion of the stratospheric ozone layer?
questions.explanation: UV light breaks down CFCs and releases chlorine atoms, which catalytically destroy ozone. This is why the Montreal Protocol phased them out.

questions.question: The Indian Naval Academy is located at:
questions.explanation: The Indian Naval Academy is at Ezhimala in the Kannur district of Kerala.

questions.question: Which is India's highest peacetime gallantry award?
questions.explanation: The Ashoka Chakra is the highest peacetime gallantry award. The Param Vir Chakra is the highest wartime award.

questions.question: How many zeros are there at the end of 100! (100 factorial)?
questions.explanation: The number of trailing zeros is ⌊100/5⌋ + ⌊100/25⌋ = 20 + 4 = 24.

questions.question: What is the remainder when 2³¹ is divided by 5?
questions.explanation: Powers of 2 mod 5 cycle as 2, 4, 3, 1 (period 4). Since 31 = 4 × 7 + 3, 2³¹ ≡ 2³ = 8 ≡ 3 (mod 5).

questions.question: The HCF of two numbers is 12 and their LCM is 360. If one number is 60, the other is:
questions.explanation: Product of the numbers = HCF × LCM, so the other number = 12 × 360 / 60 = 72. Check: HCF(60, 72) = 12 and LCM = 360.

questions.question: If the price of sugar rises by 25%, by what percentage must a family reduce its consumption so that its expenditure on sugar stays the same?
The compound interest on ₹10,000 at 10% per annum for 2 years, compounded annually, is:
A shopkeeper marks his goods 40% above the cost price and allows a discount of 10% on the marked price. His profit per cent is:
questions.explanation: SP = 1.40 × 0.90 × CP = 1.26 × CP, so the profit is 26%.

questions.question: A can complete a work in 12 days and B in 18 days. Working together, they will complete it in:
questions.explanation: Combined rate = 1/12 + 1/18 = 5/36 per day, so time = 36/5 = 7.2 days.

questions.question: A train 150 m long runs at 54 km/h. How long will it take to cross a bridge 300 m long?
questions.explanation: 54 km/h = 15 m/s. The distance to cover is 150 + 300 = 450 m, so time = 450/15 = 30 s.

questions.question: If A : B = 2 : 3 and B : C = 4 : 5, then A : B : C is:
questions.explanation: Make B common: A : B = 8 : 12 and B : C = 12 : 15, so A : B : C = 8 : 12 : 15.

questions.question: If x + 1/x = 3, then x³ + 1/x³ equals:
If a + b + c = 0, then a³ + b³ + c³ equals:
questions.explanation: a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc = (a + b + c)(a² + b² + c² − ab − bc − ca) = 0, so a³ + b³ + c³ = 3abc.

questions.question: If 2x + 3y = 12 and 3x − y = 7, then x + y equals:
questions.explanation: From the second equation, y = 3x − 7. Then 2x + 9x − 21 = 12 gives x = 3 and y = 2, so x + y = 5.

questions.question: In triangle ABC, ∠A = 50°. The bisectors of ∠B and ∠C meet at I. The measure of ∠BIC is:
Each interior angle of a regular polygon is 140°. The number of its sides is:
questions.explanation: Exterior angle = 180° − 140° = 40°, so the number of sides = 360°/40° = 9.

questions.question: A point P is 13 cm from the centre of a circle of radius 5 cm. The length of the tangent drawn from P to the circle is:
questions.explanation: The tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact, so its length = √(13² − 5²) = √144 = 12 cm.

questions.question: The total surface area of a cube is 150 cm². Its volume is:
questions.explanation: 6a² = 150 gives a = 5 cm, so the volume is a³ = 125 cm³.

questions.question: The curved surface area of a cylinder of radius 7 cm and height 10 cm is (take π = 22/7):
If sin θ = 3/5 and θ is acute, then sec θ + tan θ equals:
questions.explanation: cos θ = 4/5, so sec θ = 5/4 and tan θ = 3/4. Their sum is 8/4 = 2.

questions.question: The angle of elevation of the top of a tower 50√3 m high from a point on level ground is 60°. The distance of the point from the foot of the tower is:
The median of the data 3, 7, 9, 2, 5, 11 is:
questions.explanation: Sorted: 2, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11. With an even count, median = (5 + 7)/2 = 6.
